summary: 高祖太子继位七年，仁弱受制于吕后，长安城成于其朝，开文景休养之基。
summary_en: The heir of Gaozu reigned seven years, gentle and controlled by Empress Lü; the walls of Chang'an rose in his reign, laying the base for the Wen-Jing recovery.

bio_md:
# 汉惠帝 · 主要事迹

刘盈是[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]与吕后之子，以太子继位，时年尚幼。他承高祖之后，萧规曹随，与民休息，朝局却从第一天起便笼罩在母亲吕太后的身影之下：长安城的营建、诸侯王的来朝、匈奴的和亲，莫不有其参决，惠帝本人以仁弱著称，史书对他七年治绩的记载，远少于对吕后临朝的叙述。

即便如此，惠帝朝并非空白。除挟书律，放宽了自秦以来的文化禁令；修成长安城，使新都第一次有了完整的城郭；与匈奴继续和亲，维持了汉初的边境休养。这些举措没有宏大叙事，却为后来的文景之治铺平了地基。

惠帝崩于未央宫，年二十四，葬安陵。身后吕后立少帝，临朝称制，刘氏诸王几遭屠戮，直到[[han-wen-di|汉文帝]]入立，汉家才重归刘氏正轨。史臣评惠帝，多言其「仁弱」，而就其朝政所积而言，亦可与文帝一朝作长线对读。

> 参考：点校本《汉书》卷002《惠帝纪》、卷003《高后纪》，《史记·吕太后本纪》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Ying was the son of

and Empress Lü. He succeeded to the throne as heir apparent while still young, keeping the statutes of Xiao He and the policies of Cao Shen and resting the people. Yet from the first day his reign stood in the shadow of his mother, Empress Dowager Lü: the building of Chang'an, the visits of the feudatory kings, and the marriage alliance with the Xiongnu were all decided with her participation. The emperor himself was known for gentleness and weakness, and the histories tell us far less about his seven years of rule than about Lü's regency.

His reign was not, however, a blank. The repeal of the law against private possession of books relaxed the cultural prohibitions inherited from Qin. The completion of the walls of Chang'an gave the new capital its first full circuit of fortifications. And the continued marriage alliance with the Xiongnu preserved the frontier quiet on which early Han rested. None of these measures made a great narrative, but together they prepared the ground for the celebrated Wen-Jing recovery.

Emperor Hui died in the Weiyang Palace at the age of twenty-four and was buried at Anling. After his death Lü enthroned a young emperor and assumed the regency in her own right; the Liu kings were nearly destroyed one by one, until the accession of

returned the House of Han to its proper line. The historians called Hui "gentle and weak," yet in what his reign accumulated, he may be read against Emperor Wen's over the long term.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 2 (Benji of Emperor Hui) and ch. 3 (Benji of Empress Lü), the *Shiji* "Basic Annals of Empress Lü," and Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
